_notes: Fits the Stone Age Chronicle layout in prehistory-parchment-newspaper-plan.md. Each entry fills ONE main headline story (headline/subhead/body/closingLine/icon/image) for that page. The generic weather + berry-season filler in the small column is reused as-is across every page per the existing plan and is NOT in this file. Images are hosted on GitHub (mohamedazizhadhri-prog/la-peace-assets1), served via jsDelivr's CDN — build each image URL at render time as ASSET_BASE_URL + '/prehistory/' + imageSlug + '.jpg'.

entries.headline: FIRST OF US!
entries.subhead: STRANGE NEW TRIBE FOUND IN THE WEST
entries.body: Elders speak of a new kind of people gathering near the western cliffs, taller and sharper-browed than any seen before. Scouts say their fires burn longer and their tools cut cleaner.
entries.closingLine: "NEW BLOOD" AND "NEW FIRE" SPOKEN OF AROUND EVERY CAMP
entries.imageAlt: Line-art illustration of early human figures gathered near a cliffside camp

entries.headline: MARKS OF THE SPIRIT!
entries.subhead: TRIBE PAINTS SKIN WITH RED EARTH
entries.body: Women of the southern camp have taken to marking their arms and brows with crushed red stone. Elders say the marks call the spirits of the hunt to favor the wearer.
entries.closingLine: "RED EARTH" NOW TRADED FOR MEAT AND SHELL
entries.imageAlt: Line-art illustration of a tribesperson applying red ochre pigment to skin

entries.headline: TRIBES MARCH NORTH!
entries.subhead: ELDERS LEAD PEOPLE BEYOND THE GREAT RIVER
entries.body: Three full camps have broken from the southern lands, following the elders across the great river toward unknown country. None who left have yet sent word back.
entries.closingLine: "NEW GROUND" PROMISED, IF THE RIVER CAN BE CROSSED
entries.imageAlt: Line-art illustration of a line of travelers crossing a wide river

entries.headline: SKY TURNS BLACK!
entries.subhead: ASH RAINS FOR MANY MOONS, HUNTERS FLEE
entries.body: A mountain far to the east is said to have split the sky itself, burying the eastern hunting grounds in gray ash. The sun has not been seen clearly since.
entries.closingLine: "THE LONG DARK" — TRIBES RATION MEAT AND WAIT
entries.imageAlt: Line-art illustration of tribespeople fleeing beneath a darkened, ash-filled sky

entries.headline: RAFT-TRIBE REACHES FAR SHORE!
entries.subhead: BRAVEST HUNTERS CROSS THE ENDLESS WATER
entries.body: After many days lashed to logs and reed, the coastal tribe's raft party has sighted land where none was known to be. They report the shore thick with unfamiliar game.
entries.closingLine: "NEW WATERS" NOW OPEN TO ANY WHO DARE THEM
entries.imageAlt: Line-art illustration of a simple raft crossing open water toward a distant shore

entries.headline: BEASTS PAINTED ON STONE!
entries.subhead: SHAMAN'S HAND MARKS THE CAVE WALL
entries.body: Deep in the eastern cave, the shaman has pressed a hand in red pigment beside a herd of painted beasts. Tribe members now make the journey to see it by torchlight.
entries.closingLine: "THE HAND MARK" SAID TO CARRY THE SHAMAN'S POWER
entries.imageAlt: Line-art illustration of a hand stencil and painted animal herd on a cave wall

entries.headline: LIONS ON THE CAVE WALL!
entries.subhead: ARTIST TRIBE PAINTS GREAT BEASTS
entries.body: The northern cave now holds painted lions, rhinos, and bears, larger and more lifelike than any seen before. Elders call it the finest cave art in living memory.
entries.closingLine: "THE GREAT GALLERY" DRAWS VISITORS FROM FAR CAMPS
entries.imageAlt: Line-art illustration of painted lions and rhinos on a cave wall

entries.headline: SONG FROM BONE!
entries.subhead: HUNTER CARVES MUSIC FOR THE FIRE
entries.body: An old hunter has hollowed a vulture's bone into a whistling pipe, drawing a clear song from it by the fire each night. Children now beg him to play before sleep.
entries.closingLine: "BONE SONG" NOW PART OF EVERY FIRESIDE GATHERING
entries.imageAlt: Line-art illustration of a hunter playing a carved bone flute beside a campfire

entries.headline: STONE MOTHER CARVED!
entries.subhead: TRIBE HONORS THE GIVER OF LIFE
entries.body: A carver of the western camp has shaped a small stone figure of a full-bodied woman, said to honor the mothers of the tribe and call for a strong birthing season.
entries.closingLine: "THE STONE MOTHER" NOW CARRIED BY THE ELDEST WOMEN
entries.imageAlt: Line-art illustration of a small carved stone figurine

entries.headline: THE COLD DEEPENS!
entries.subhead: ICE SWALLOWS THE NORTHERN HUNTING GROUNDS
entries.body: Scouts report the northern ice has crept further south than any elder remembers, burying the old reindeer trails. Tribes are being forced toward the warmer southern coasts.
entries.closingLine: "THE DEEP COLD" — SOUTHERN CAMPS PREPARE FOR NEW ARRIVALS
entries.imageAlt: Line-art illustration of an ice-covered landscape with a distant line of migrating figures

entries.headline: GREAT HALL OF BULLS FOUND!
entries.subhead: DEEP CAVE HOLDS HUNDRED PAINTED BEASTS
entries.body: Boys chasing a lost dog have found a hidden cave whose walls are covered top to bottom with painted bulls, horses, and stags. Elders say no living painter could have made them all.
entries.closingLine: "THE BULL HALL" NOW FORBIDDEN TO ALL BUT THE SHAMANS
entries.imageAlt: Line-art illustration of a cave chamber covered in painted bulls and horses

entries.headline: NEW LAND ACROSS THE ICE BRIDGE!
entries.subhead: TRIBES WALK WHERE NO FOOT HAS TROD
entries.body: Hunters following mammoth herds across the frozen northern land-bridge report open, game-rich country on the far side, with no sign any people have hunted it before.
entries.closingLine: "UNCLAIMED GROUND" — WHOLE CAMPS NOW PREPARE TO CROSS
entries.imageAlt: Line-art illustration of hunters and mammoths crossing an icy land bridge

entries.headline: THE LONG WINTER BREAKS!
entries.subhead: ICE RETREATS, RIVERS RUN FREE AGAIN
entries.body: After a lifetime of deep cold, elders say the northern ice is finally pulling back. Rivers long frozen solid now run free, and green is returning to ground bare for generations.
entries.closingLine: "THE THAW" — OLDEST TRIBE MEMBERS CALL IT A SIGN
entries.imageAlt: Line-art illustration of melting ice and a river running through a greening landscape

entries.headline: GREAT STONE CIRCLE RAISED!
entries.subhead: TRIBES GATHER TO BUILD A TEMPLE OF STONE
entries.body: Camps from across the hill country have joined to raise a ring of carved stone pillars taller than three men, said to be for gathering and worship rather than shelter.
entries.closingLine: "THE STONE RING" DRAWS TRIBES FROM MANY DAYS' WALK
entries.imageAlt: Line-art illustration of carved stone pillars arranged in a circle

entries.headline: SEEDS SOWN IN ROWS!
entries.subhead: TRIBE PLANTS WHEAT INSTEAD OF SEEKING IT
entries.body: Rather than gathering wild grain as it's found, the river-plain tribe has taken to pressing seed into cleared rows of earth by hand, and tending the ground until it ripens.
entries.closingLine: "PLANTED GRAIN" — ELDERS DIVIDED ON WHETHER IT WILL LAST
entries.imageAlt: Line-art illustration of a figure sowing seeds into cleared rows of earth

entries.headline: WILD GOAT TAMED!
entries.subhead: HERD NOW FOLLOWS THE TRIBE, NOT THE HUNTER
entries.body: A young herder has raised a band of wild goats from kids, and reports the animals now follow the camp of their own will rather than fleeing at the hunt.
entries.closingLine: "THE FOLLOWING HERD" — TRIBE NO LONGER MUST TRACK ITS MEAT
entries.imageAlt: Line-art illustration of a herder walking alongside a small herd of goats

entries.headline: ROOFTOP CITY RISES!
entries.subhead: HUNDREDS NOW LIVE WALL TO WALL ON THE PLAIN
entries.body: The plain settlement has grown so dense that homes now share walls, with families entering by ladder through the roof rather than by any door. Elders count it the largest camp ever gathered.
entries.closingLine: "THE ROOFTOP TOWN" NOW HOME TO MORE THAN ANY SINGLE TRIBE
entries.imageAlt: Line-art illustration of densely packed flat-roofed dwellings with rooftop entrances

entries.headline: CLAY HARDENED BY FIRE!
entries.subhead: TRIBE STORES GRAIN IN BAKED EARTH JARS
entries.body: Potters of the river camp have found that shaped clay, left long enough in the fire, hardens into vessels that hold grain and water without cracking or leaking.
entries.closingLine: "FIRED CLAY" — NO MORE GRAIN LOST TO DAMP OR RATS
entries.imageAlt: Line-art illustration of clay pots being fired beside a hearth

entries.headline: ROUND STONE ROLLS TRUE!
entries.subhead: CARTWRIGHT'S WHEEL CARRIES LOAD WITHOUT LEGS
entries.body: A craftsman has fitted a round cut stone to an axle beneath a sled, and reports it drags a full load of grain with far less strain than any ox or back could manage alone.
entries.closingLine: "THE ROLLING STONE" — EVERY CAMP NOW WANTS ONE BUILT
entries.imageAlt: Line-art illustration of an early cart fitted with a round wheel

entries.headline: MARKS THAT SPEAK!
entries.subhead: SCRIBES OF SUMER PRESS WORDS INTO CLAY
entries.body: Temple scribes have taken to pressing wedge-shaped marks into wet clay tablets to record grain counts and trade, said to hold meaning even after the speaker has left.
entries.closingLine: "THE WEDGE MARKS" — WORDS THAT OUTLAST THE VOICE
entries.imageAlt: Line-art illustration of a scribe pressing wedge-shaped marks into a clay tablet
